To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a planning-based approach to web service composition is feasible, (ii) it is possible to customize web service compositions to individual preferences, and (iii) the resulting customized compositions are sound and efficient.

(i) we have developed the theoretical foundations of a planning-based framework for WSC that is based on a novel representation of preferences and that enables the composition of plans that satisfy preferences, and (ii) we have demonstrated that this framework can be implemented to solve a range of WSC problems.

we have developed a formalism for the representation of preferences in the context of WSC, that we have shown this formalism to be expressive enough to represent the preferences of a wide class of users, and that we have developed an algorithm to automatically generate a plan that satisfies the preferences of a user, given the preferences of the user, the user's objective, and a set of services.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(a) the customization of WSC with respect to preferences over the composition of services; (b) the integration of WSC into an open, distributed environment; and (c) the development of efficient algorithms for planning in the presence of preferences.
